name: sharp_rademacher_singularity_conjecture
statement: For $B_n$ an $n\times n$ iid uniform $\{-1,+1\}$ matrix, $\Pr(\det B_n=0)=(1+o(1))\,2n^2 2^{-n}$. Tag (1).
notes: S1 opens by declaring the conjecture NOT proved in the checkpoint (S1 lines 12-13). S1 line 58 records the published sharp upper bound as still open, citing Sahasrabudhe's survey (arXiv 2512.15077v1), Tikhomirov's $2^{-n+o(n)}$ theorem (Annals 191-2 p06), and the Jain-Sah-Sawhney structured/unstructured reduction (arXiv 2010.06554). Nothing in S1-S5 claims (1).

name: entropy_defect_ell
statement: For a spanning antipodal sign fibre $A\subseteq\{\pm1\}^r$, the entropy defect is $\ell(A)=r-\log_2|A|$.
notes: Real-valued, not integer. Used throughout S1 as the entropy budget that all batching charges must fit inside.

name: d_cb_signed_selector_residual_rank
statement: $d_{\rm cb}(A)$ is the minimum signed-selector residual rank after optimizing over coordinate bases in the full dual: choose a coordinate basis from the full dual and signed selectors so that ALL assignment residuals lie in one common space $R$; minimize $\dim R$ over basis and selectors.
notes: Always $d_{\rm geo}\le d_{\rm cb}$. Equality holds for the rooted-NAE cycle family at high corank (see rooted_nae_cycle_exact_dcb).

name: d_geo_signed_projective_class_distance
statement: With $C\in\mathbb R^{3\times m}$ of rank 3, $S_t=\{x\in\{\pm1\}^m:Cx=t\}$, $W=\ker C$, $r=\dim W=m-3$, $f_i=x_i|_W\in W^*$: a geometric residual is $R=\operatorname{span}\{f_i-\sigma f_j:\sigma\in\{\pm1\}\}\le W^*$; $k_F(R)$ counts signed projective classes of the $f_i$ modulo $R$ (all forms lying in $R$ count as one zero class); $d_{\rm geo}(F)=\min\{\dim R:k_F(R)\le r\}$. Tag (1) of S5.
notes: This is the canonical precise definition in the assigned range; S1 uses the same notion informally. Field: $\mathbb R$.

name: global_bridge_exponential_dcb_bound
statement: $\boxed{d_{\rm cb}(A)\le 9\cdot4^{\ell(A)}+\ell(A)}$ for a full-closed spanning antipodal fibre $A\subseteq\{\pm1\}^r$. Tag (2)/(19).
source: dossier p.55 (S1 line 18); proof dossier pp.60-63 (S1 lines 261-365)
notes: S1 line 29-31: a genuine global theorem but EXPONENTIAL, not linear, in $\ell$. It extends the already-summable determinant range but does not bridge the full endpoint. Proof is analytic and uniform; the finite searches are adversarial checks only.

name: linear_rigidity_target_3
statement: The sharp deterministic theorem still missing: $\boxed{d_{\rm cb}(A)\le C\,\ell(A)}$ for an absolute constant $C$, together with a connector-compatible conditional version. Tag (3).
notes: NOT disproved by any object in S1-S5; the crosspolytope and the rooted-NAE cycle family are both consistent with a linear bound. The rooted-NAE family forces any valid $C\ge1.090186\ldots$ asymptotically and $C\ge5/3.9749=1.2579$ already at $n=13$.

name: layer_three_transfer_still_unwritten
statement: Even after (3), the required-order centered-moment / Jain-Sah-Sawhney transfer must still be written at the random-normal endpoint. Neither the finite audits nor (2) should be described as a proof of (1).
notes: Explicit honesty statement by the source itself. This is the Layer-III residual: a deterministic rigidity theorem alone does not close the conjecture.

name: rooted_connector_target_41
statement: The form needed by the recursive block tree: with $R_<\subseteq\operatorname{span}W$ the residual space already paid by ancestors, one needs selectors with $\dim\frac{R+R_<}{R_<}\le C\,L_{Q\mid W}$ AND $R\cap\operatorname{span}W\subseteq R_<$. Tag (41). The first inequality is conditional linear rigidity; the second is connector absorption. Under both, conditional defects telescope without a depth loss.
notes: This is THE named gap of the whole programme. Absorption is a separate clause, not implied by the rank bound; see nae_three_arm_star_absorption_counterexample.

name: first_uncovered_homogeneous_block_class
statement: The first homogeneous block not covered by the audited local theorems is a singleton-layer cyclic SCC of relation corank at least five which is not a rooted-NAE cycle (nor one of the previously solved stable-set, median, or paired-Gale classes), and which either has unbounded entropy-normalized batching congestion (at least order $\log n$ in the endpoint range) in every useful junction basis, or fails the common-lift condition (24e).
notes: Note the disjunction: unbounded $\kappa$ OR absorption failure. Corank threshold is 'at least five'. Combined with the polylog-density corollary, the residual class has genuinely polylogarithmically dense rows.

name: next_subproblem_witness_basis_iteration
statement: Starting from the witness basis (28), either (a) find a batching with $\kappa=O(1)$ and verify the common-lift condition (24e), or (b) use the unused part of the conditional defect to extract further dense witnesses until the remainder has bounded congestion. Any connector dependency exposed in that iteration must be assigned to a paid fundamental cycle or split off as a lower block.
notes: S1's own explicit warning attached to this route: 'The crosspolytope shows that the remainder may retain essentially all of $\ell$ even when the first batching has only one witness.' So route (b) has no a priori progress measure.

name: falsified_tools_list_S1
statement: The following tools are already falsified and must not be used in the remaining programme: universal pair branching; monotonicity under row deletion; saturation of a geometric optimizer; per-ear entropy charging; bare matroid $2$-sum factorization across a nonbinary separator.
notes: S1 gives no counterexample for each individually in this file; it states them as already-settled negatives from the preceding project tree. Treat as a do-not-retry list, not as re-derivable here.

name: two_shadow_graph_Gamma
statement: Let $h_a\in\mathbb R^r$ and $S=\{x\in\{\pm1\}^r:h_a\cdot x\in\{\pm1\}\ \forall a\}$, $|S|=2^{r-\ell}$ (tag 12). Delete rows already equal to signed coordinates, put $E_a=\operatorname{supp}h_a$. The two-shadow graph $\Gamma$ on $[r]$ has $ij\in E(\Gamma)$ when some $E_a$ contains both $i$ and $j$.
notes: The row deletion step is essential: rows already equal to signed coordinates carry no two-shadow.

name: weighted_two_shadow_compression_thm_5_1
statement: There is a vertex cover $C\subseteq[r]$ of $\Gamma$ with $\boxed{|C|\le 9\cdot4^{\ell}}$ (tag 13) such that every $E_a$ contains at most one coordinate outside $C$.
source: dossier p.60 (S1 lines 261-266); proof pp.60-62 (S1 lines 273-320)
notes: $|C|=2N$ where $N$ is the size of a maximum matching in $\Gamma$; $N\le(9/2)4^\ell$. The endpoints of a maximum matching form a vertex cover, which is what gives the 'at most one coordinate outside $C$' property.

name: greedy_batching_peel_method
statement: Take a maximum matching $P_1,\dots,P_N$ in $\Gamma$. Greedily choose a remaining pair, a witness row $E_s$ containing it, and remove the batch $B_s$ of all remaining matching pairs meeting $E_s$; put $a_s=|B_s|$. Batches partition the matching. With $V_s$ the endpoints of $B_s$ and $U_s=E_s\cap V_s$: $|U_s|\ge a_s+1$ (tag 14), the $U_s$ are disjoint, and $E_s$ avoids every later $U_t$. Condition outside $\bigcup_s U_s$ and peel $U_k,\dots,U_1$ in reverse exposure order.
notes: Key independence bookkeeping: earlier selected row indicators are independent of the set being peeled, and variables in earlier $U_t$'s are held as arbitrary parameters. This is exactly why the Littlewood-Offord input must be TARGET-UNIFORM (two-point form).

name: psi_batching_charge_inequalities
statement: $2^{-\ell}\le\prod_s\psi(a_s+1)$ (tag 15) where $\psi(u)=\min\{3/4,\,2^{1-u}\binom{u}{\lfloor u/2\rfloor}\}\le\min\{3/4,\,2/\sqrt u\}$ (tag 16). With $c_s=-\log_2\psi(a_s+1)$ and $\beta=\log_2(4/3)$: $c_s\ge\beta$, $\sum_s c_s\le\ell$, $a_s+1\le4\cdot4^{c_s}$ (tag 17). Since $4^\beta=16/9$, $\sum_s4^{c_s}\le\frac98 4^{\sum_s c_s}\le\frac98 4^{\ell}$ (tag 18).
notes: VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY (this campaign, 2026-08-19, exact arithmetic): $4^{\log_2(4/3)}=(4/3)^2=16/9$; $a_s+1\le4\cdot4^{c_s}$ follows from $\psi\le2/\sqrt u$; and the constant $9/8$ in (18) is EXACTLY the worst case $N=2$ of $\sum x_s/\prod x_s$ over $x_s\ge16/9$ (N=1 gives 1, N=2 gives 1.125, N=3 gives 0.949). Also $c_s\ge\max\{\beta,\tfrac12\log_2(a_s+1)-1\}$ (S1 line 507).

name: entropy_sharpened_residual_rank_thm_5_2
statement: If $S$ is nonempty and antipodal then, for the fixed input basis, $\boxed{d(H)\le 9\cdot4^{\ell}+\ell}$ (tag 19). Proof: every row is $h_a(x)=q_a(x_C)+\lambda_a x_j$ for at most one $j\notin C$ (tag 20); if $j$ is conditionally free (both signs of $X_j$ occur above some realized core value $X_C=c$) then $q_a(c)=0$ and $\lambda_a=\pm1$ (tag 21), so selecting $\lambda_a x_j$ leaves a core-supported residual. If $N_0$ is the never-free outside set, $X_{N_0}$ is a deterministic function of $X_C$, giving $|N_0|\le\ell-(|C|-H(X_C))\le\ell$ (tag 22).
notes: All residuals lie in the coordinate span of $C\cup N_0$, hence dimension $\le|C|+|N_0|\le9\cdot4^\ell+\ell$. The entropy step uses $r-\ell=H(X)\le H(X_C)+r-|C|-|N_0|$ for uniform $X\in S$. The free/never-free dichotomy is the reusable part.

name: conditional_entropy_defect_L_QW
statement: If $W$ is a sign boundary and $Q$ a private sign basis of size $q$, the conditional entropy defect is $L_{Q\mid W}=q-H(Q\mid W)$. Tag (23).
notes: Real-valued and can be arbitrarily small (see one_private_vertex_interval_no_defect_only_bound). $H$ is in bits; $Q$ conditioned on the boundary variables.

name: conditional_exponential_quotient_bound_24
statement: The same target-uniform proof yields selectors whose new residual rank modulo the boundary is $\boxed{\dim\frac{R+\operatorname{span}W}{\operatorname{span}W}\le 9\cdot4^{L_{Q\mid W}}+L_{Q\mid W}}$. Tag (24).
notes: S1 lines 385-387 state explicitly: this does NOT ensure $R\cap\operatorname{span}W$ was already paid by the parent; that connector-absorption clause is a separate part of the remaining theorem.

name: kappa_entropy_normalized_congestion
statement: $\kappa=\max_s\dfrac{a_s}{c_s}$ with $c_s=-\log_2\psi(a_s+1)$. Tag (24a).
notes: Entropy-NORMALIZED congestion: a batch is cheap not when it is small but when its size is proportional to the entropy it consumes. $\kappa$ is basis- and batching-dependent, which is why the residual class is defined by 'in every useful basis'.

name: bounded_congestion_linear_rigidity_thm_5_3
statement: For the conditional block of (23), $\sum_s c_s\le L_{Q\mid W}$ and $N=\sum_s a_s\le\kappa L_{Q\mid W}$ (tag 24b); the matching endpoints give a private core of size $\le2\kappa L_{Q\mid W}$, and the free/never-free entropy step adds $\le L_{Q\mid W}$ further private directions, whence $\boxed{\dim\frac{R+\operatorname{span}W}{\operatorname{span}W}\le(2\kappa+1)L_{Q\mid W}}$. Tag (24c)/(2a).
notes: Independently audited PASS per the S1 ledger. This is a QUOTIENT-rank bound only; it carries no absorption clause. Corollary: if every selected witness has private support $\le s$ then $\kappa\le(s-1)/\beta$, giving the absolute coefficient $1+2(s-1)/\beta$; so every bounded-support homogeneous high-corank block satisfies genuine linear rigidity. Exchanging selected witnesses into the coordinate basis costs a further $L_{Q\mid W}/\beta$ (S1 lines 416-421).

name: absorption_kernel_criterion_24e
statement: Write residual generators as $r_a=b_a+p_a$ (boundary part $b_a$, private part $p_a$) and set $P(e_a)=p_a$, $\overline B(e_a)=b_a+R_<$ (tag 24d). Then $\boxed{R\cap\operatorname{span}W\subseteq R_<\iff\ker P\subseteq\ker\overline B\iff\overline B=T\circ P\text{ for some linear }T}$. Tag (24e).
notes: EXACT algebraic certificate for the missing absorption clause; this is the 'common linear lift' condition. Any displayed kernel basis is a finite certificate. S1 line 443: bounded congestion PLUS paid cycle sums is a complete connector-ready linear theorem.

name: fundamental_cycle_basis_absorption_test
statement: For a network residual matrix it is enough to check (24e) on a fundamental-cycle basis: every pure boundary dependency arising from private cancellation must be an ancestor-paid cycle sum.
notes: Reduces an infinite-looking condition to a finite check of size = cyclomatic number. This is the graphic/network structural certificate; for blocks with full-column-rank $P$ (private anchors), $\ker P=0$ and absorption is automatic.

name: nae_three_arm_star_absorption_counterexample
statement: The fully closed three-arm NAE star $Y_i=x_i+z_i+q$ ($1\le i\le3$) with $W=(x_i,z_i)_{i=1}^3$, $Q=(q)$ (tag 24f) has $L_{Q\mid W}=19/27$ and private support one, yet EVERY boundary-preserving sign basis and selector choice creates a nonzero pure boundary residual when $R_<=0$. Hence neither bounded support nor bounded incidence degree implies (24e).
notes: VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY (this campaign, exact enumeration): the fibre has $|A|=54$ points, the boundary $(x,z)$ support has 46 elements ($27+27-8$), $H(Q\mid W)=8/27$, so $L_{Q\mid W}=1-8/27=19/27=0.7037\ldots$ exactly. S1's conclusion: the surviving hypothesis must encode CYCLIC CONNECTOR COHERENCE, not sparsity alone. Proof of the forced leak is in structured_linear_rigidity_report.md, which is NOT reproduced in this page range.

name: endpoint_encoding_exponent_25
statement: For a rank-$r$, size-$k$ component, the existing ternary basis-mass encoding has exponent $-(n-r)\ell+O\bigl(d_{\rm cb}k+(k-r)\log r+r+n\bigr)$. Tag (25).
notes: This is the Layer-II/Layer-III interface: only $d_{\rm cb}$ enters, multiplied by $k$. Everything the deterministic rigidity programme buys enters the endpoint through this one term.

name: endpoint_gain_from_exponential_bridge
statement: With (19), every component sequence with $k=O(n/\log n)$, $\ell\to\infty$, and $4^{\ell}=o(\ell\log n)$ (tag 26) has the required exponential saving. Hence any sequence not covered by (26) has a subsequence on which $4^\ell\gtrsim\ell\log n$, and there, up to constants, $\ell\ge\tfrac12\log_2\log n+\tfrac12\log_2\log\log n-O(1)$ (tag 27).
notes: Fixed $\ell$ was already handled by the fixed-core enumeration. This improves the previous $O((1+\ell)4^\ell)$ common-core range but does NOT cover all admissible $\ell$. Verified: $4^\ell\gtrsim\ell\log n$ gives $2\ell\ge\log_2\log n+\log_2\ell$, consistent with (27).

name: endpoint_gain_from_bounded_congestion
statement: In the same range $k=O(n/\log n)$ one has $n-r=(1-o(1))n$, while (24c) contributes $O(\kappa\ell k)=O\!\left(\frac{\kappa}{\log n}n\ell\right)$ to the encoding exponent (tag 27a). Hence every homogeneous component sequence admitting a batching with $\kappa=o(\log n)$ (tag 27b) also has the required saving.
notes: Orthogonal to (26). Fixed-defect cases handled separately. This is the arithmetic behind the campaign's transfer-lane observation that any UNIFORM coefficient $o(\log n)$ suffices at the endpoint interface -- an absolute constant is strictly more than the moment bookkeeping consumes.

name: residual_obstruction_is_polylog_dense
statement: An unresolved nonsummable sequence must simultaneously lie beyond (26) and have $\kappa\gtrsim\log n$ in every useful basis. Since $c_s\ge\max\{\beta,\tfrac12\log_2(a_s+1)-1\}$, such a batching contains a witness meeting $\Omega(\log n\log\log n)$ disjoint matching pairs; the surviving core therefore has genuinely polylogarithmically dense rows, not merely unbounded support.
notes: This is the sharpest available characterization of the residual class in pp.55-112: 'a substantially denser obstruction than arbitrary high corank'. Both conditions are required simultaneously.

name: simultaneous_witness_basis_exchange_28
statement: Let $E_1,\dots,E_k$ be the selected witness rows in deletion order; from each witness pair choose one pivot $p_s\in E_s$. The pivots are distinct and $E_s$ contains no later pivot $p_t$ ($t>s$), so $(h_s(p_t))_{s,t=1}^k$ is triangular with nonzero diagonal. Hence $\boxed{\{h_1,\dots,h_k\}\cup\{e_i:i\notin\{p_1,\dots,p_k\}\}\text{ is a coordinate basis}}$ (tag 28), and $k\le\ell/\log_2(4/3)$ (tag 29).
notes: All selected dense witnesses can be inserted simultaneously after only $O(\ell)$ basis exchanges. $1/\log_2(4/3)=2.4094208\ldots$ appears here as an UPPER-bound coefficient on the witness count -- do NOT conflate it with the S6 (p.113) LOWER floor $C\ge1/\log_2(4/3)$ from NAE three-circuit products, which is a different statement outside this page range.

name: walsh_crosspolytope_batching_insufficient
statement: For $r=2^{2t}$ let $H$ be Walsh-Hadamard and $A_r=\{\pm H_{*j}:1\le j\le r\}$ (tag 30), a fully closed crosspolytope fibre with projective full dual $\{\frac1r Hv:v\in\{\pm1\}^r\}/\{\pm1\}$. A bent $v$ has full Walsh support, so one admissible form witnesses a single batch containing an entire perfect matching and the exchange (28) is legal with $k=1$. Nevertheless $d_{\rm cb}(A_r)=r-\lfloor\log_2(2r)\rfloor$ for every coordinate basis (tag 31).
notes: DISPROVES the tempting conclusion that after the witness exchange the unselected rows cost only $O(k)$, or only $O(\sum_s c_s)$, residual directions. NOT a counterexample to linear rigidity: here $\ell=r-\log_2(2r)$, so (31) is exactly of order $\ell$. Moral (S1 line 573-575): a successful proof must allocate the UNUSED GLOBAL DEFECT after the witness exchange, not just count batches or selected-row atom losses.

name: crosspolytope_quotient_counting_lemma
statement: A residual quotient of dimension $q=r-d$ maps the full dual to at most the $2r$ signed selector images, while a rank-$q$ linear image of the cube has at least $2^q$ images; hence $2^q\le2r$, i.e. $d\ge r-\lfloor\log_2(2r)\rfloor$. The matching upper construction attains equality.
notes: Clean reusable lower-bound technique: count images of the cube under the quotient against the number of available signed selector classes.

name: rooted_nae_cycle_fibre
statement: For $n\ge4$, $A_n=\{(a,b_1,\dots,b_n)\in\{\pm1\}^{n+1}: a+b_i+b_{i+1}\in\{\pm1\}\ \forall i\}$ with cyclic indices (tag 32). On the half $a=1$ the vertices with $b_i=1$ form an independent set of $C_n$; the other half is antipodal. Hence $|A_n|=2L_n$ and $\ell(A_n)=n-\log_2 L_n$ (tag 33), $L_n$ the $n$th Lucas number. The fibre is full closed with projective full dual exactly $D_n=\{A,B_i,C_i\}$, $A=e_0$, $B_i=e_i$, $C_i=e_0+e_i+e_{i+1}$ (tag 34).
notes: Ambient rank $r=n+1$, so $\ell=(n+1)-\log_2(2L_n)=n-\log_2 L_n$. VERIFIED: $L_{13}=521$, $\ell(A_{13})=3.97486\ldots$; $|D_n|=2n+1$.

name: rooted_nae_cycle_exact_dcb
statement: For every $n\ge4$, $\boxed{d_{\rm cb}(A_n)=d_{\rm geo}(A_n)=\lceil n/3\rceil}$. Tag (35).
notes: Uniform in $n$; the proof does not depend on enumeration. This is the exact solution of a genuine high-corank cyclic family, in precisely the activation-and-connector form the recursive programme needs.

name: binary_quotient_lemma_S_n
statement: Put $\mathcal S_n=\{0\}\cup\{u_i\}\cup\{u_i+u_{i+1}\}\subseteq\mathbb F_2^n$. For every $w$-dimensional subspace $W$, $\boxed{|\mathcal S_n/W|\ge2n+1-3w}$ (tag 36). For a real signed-difference residual $R$ of dimension $d$, replace $R$ by the rational span $R_0\subseteq R$ of its actual class witnesses ($d_0=\dim R_0\le d$) and reduce the saturated lattice $R_0\cap\mathbb Z^{n+1}$ modulo two; signed equality becomes ordinary coset equality, giving $k_{D_n}(R)\ge2n+1-3d_0\ge2n+1-3d$ (tag 37).
notes: Proof of (36): choose $n-w$ coordinate images forming a quotient basis; removing the other $w$ cycle vertices destroys at most $2w$ cycle edges, so at least $n-2w$ distinct weight-two basis sums remain, plus zero and the $n-w$ singleton images. The REAL-to-$\mathbb F_2$ passage (saturated lattice mod 2) is the reusable trick; it is what makes a real residual bound follow from a binary counting bound.

name: rooted_nae_selector_upper_construction
statement: Choose an independent dominating set $U\subseteq C_n$ of size $d=\lceil n/3\rceil$ whose cyclic gaps all have length two or three; put $L_u=A+B_u$ and $R=\operatorname{span}\{L_u:u\in U\}$ (tag 38a). Orient the cycle; in every gap $u-v-u'$ choose $B_v,C_v$, in every gap $u-v-w-u'$ choose $B_v,C_v,C_w$. With $A$ these are $n+1$ full-dual forms forming a coordinate basis (backward substitution: $B_{u'}$ occurs uniquely in the last $C$-form of the preceding gap). Modulo $R$: $B_u\equiv-A$, $C_u\equiv B_v$, and $B_w\equiv C_w$ in a length-three gap (tag 38b).
notes: Every member of $D_n$ has a signed representative in this basis and every selector residual lies in the independent $d$-space $R$, proving $d_{\rm cb}\le d$. Matching lower-bound counting: cliques of $C_n-U$ number at most $1+(n-|U|)+(n-2|U|)=2n+1-3|U|\le n+1$ (tag 38).

name: rooted_nae_activation_cell_inequality
statement: For $Z_u=1_{\{L_u\ne0\}}$ and every $z\in\{0,1\}^U$, $\boxed{|(A_n)_z|\le2^{\,n+1-d-|z|}}$ (tag 38c). Consequently $|A_n|/2^{n+1}\le(3/4)^d$ and $d\le\ell(A_n)/\log_2(4/3)$ (tag 38d).
notes: Proof: on the $a=1$ half, $Z$ records the intersection of an independent set of $C_n$ with $U$. A length-two gap has $2,1,1$ completions according as its two endpoint states have sum $0,1,2$; a length-three gap has $3,2,1$. These are bounded by $2^{g-1-(s+t)/2}$; multiplying over gaps yields $2^{n-d-|z|}$, and antipodality supplies (38c). This is the STRONGER cellwise form the recursive programme wants, not merely a rank bound.

name: rooted_nae_connector_compatibility_38e
statement: If $A$ is treated as the incoming boundary and the $B_i$ as private coordinates, projection sends $L_u$ to the independent private coordinate $B_u$. Therefore $R\cap\operatorname{span}\{A\}=0$ (tag 38e): the optimal cyclic certificate is connector-compatible with no boundary surcharge.
notes: This is a POSITIVE absorption instance: zero connector intersection, so absorption holds trivially with $R_<=0$. Contrast the NAE STAR, where absorption fails at $R_<=0$. Both are NAE structures; the difference is cyclic connector coherence, not sparsity.

name: rooted_nae_path_and_interval_constants
statement: For the rooted-NAE path on $N$ vertices, $d_{\rm cb}=d_{\rm geo}=\lceil(N-1)/3\rceil$ (tag 38f). If its root and two endpoints are boundary and the $m=N-2$ interior vertices are private, there is a boundary-preserving basis with $d_m=\lceil(m+1)/3\rceil$ and $R_m\cap\operatorname{span}W=0$ (tag 38g). For every $m\ge2$, $d_m\le C_{\rm int}L_{Q\mid W}$ with the sharp uniform coefficient $C_{\rm int}=\frac{2}{3-\log_2 5}=2.949539\ldots$ (tag 38h).
notes: VERIFIED: $2/(3-\log_2 5)=2.9495396947\ldots$. The stronger activation coefficient $1/\beta=2.40942\ldots$ holds for $m=2$ and every $m\ge4$; the three-vertex neutral interval ($m=3$) is the genuine five-point cellwise exception. Proofs in rooted_nae_selector_connector_report.md (not reproduced in pp.55-112).

name: one_private_vertex_interval_no_defect_only_bound
statement: For $m=1$ (one private interior vertex), NO defect-only bound is possible: $L_{Q\mid W}$ can tend to zero while one new direction remains. However the block costs zero once its two boundary residuals have been ancestor-paid.
notes: CRITICAL for the shape of (41): this is why the absorption clause cannot be dropped from the statement -- it is forced into it, not optional. It also shows the two-regime structure: defect-poor blocks can never be charged locally, but they admit exactly-absorbed alternatives once ancestors have paid. Note the caveat 'once its two boundary residuals have been ancestor-paid' -- the bookkeeping semantics matter.

name: rooted_nae_dual_matroid_three_connected
statement: The real full-dual matroid on $D_n$ is genuinely three-connected. A dual representation is $t=\sum_i e_i$, $p_i=e_i$, $q_i=e_i+e_{i+1}$. A run-count proof shows every partition $(X,Y)$ with $|X|,|Y|\ge2$ satisfies $r(X)+r(Y)-n\ge2$; every dual column is nonzero and deleting any one column leaves rank $n$, ruling out singleton one-separations.
notes: Run-count proof lives in rigidity_attack_report.md, not reproduced here. This object exists to certify that the family below is genuinely three-connected, which is what makes it a counterexample rather than a degenerate case.

name: three_connected_ceiling_lemma_disproved
statement: The candidate '$d_{\rm cb}(A)\le\lceil\ell(A)\rceil$ for three-connected full-dual blocks' is FALSE. Already $n=13$ gives $d_{\rm cb}(A_{13})=d_{\rm geo}(A_{13})=5>\lceil13-\log_2 521\rceil=4$ (tag 39); every $n\equiv0\pmod 6$, $n\ge42$ gives an infinite counterexample subfamily. Equivalently, the fixed-$q$ evaluation-Rado proposal fails in genuine three-connected blocks.
notes: VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY: $\ell(A_{13})=13-\log_2 521=3.97486$, $\lceil\cdot\rceil=4$, while $\lceil13/3\rceil=5$. Consequence stated by S1: three-connectivity cannot be used as a ZERO-WORK ceiling certificate; a high-corank block must pay a positive entropy cost internally. It does NOT threaten an absolute linear theorem.

name: rooted_nae_ratio_limit_1_0902
statement: $\dfrac{d_{\rm cb}(A_n)}{\ell(A_n)}\longrightarrow\dfrac{1}{3(1-\log_2\varphi)}=1.090186\ldots$ as $n\to\infty$, $\varphi$ the golden ratio. Tag (40).
notes: VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY: $\log_2\varphi=0.6942419$, $1/(3\cdot0.3057581)=1.0901865$. Finite values approach from ABOVE: $n=4$ gives $2/1.19265=1.6769$; $n=13$ gives $5/3.97486=1.2579$. name: scalar_gaps_target_uniform
statement: For twelve nonzero coefficients, an affine atom which is not the central atom of twelve equal magnitudes has size at most $792$. name: zero_gale_column_deletion_lemma
statement: Suppose $c_1=0$; write $C'=(c_2,\dots,c_m)$, $S'_t=\{x'\in\{\pm1\}^{m-1}:C'x'=t\}$, $W'=\ker C'$. Then $S_t=\{\pm1\}\times S'_t$ and $|S_t|/2^m=|S'_t|/2^{m-1}$ (tag 4); moreover every dimension-$d$ residual certificate for the reduced family lifts to a dimension-$d$ certificate for the original, so $d_{\rm geo}(F')\le2\Rightarrow d_{\rm geo}(F)\le2$ (tag 5). Corollary: deleting all zero Gale columns preserves the affine atom density, and if the unreduced family is projectively simple with $d_{\rm geo}(F)=3$ then the reduced family also has $d_{\rm geo}=3$.
source: dossier pp.104-105 (S5 lines 57-108); dossier p.91 (S3 lines 288-290); dossier p.60 (S1 lines 227-228)
notes: Proof: $W=\mathbb Re_1\oplus W'$, $r=1+r'$; regarding $R'$ as $0\oplus R'$, the reduced forms occupy $\le r'$ classes and the free coordinate $e_1^*$ adds at most one, so $k_F(R)\le r'+1=r$. The corollary's exactness uses that three signed forest edges always give a residual of dimension $\le3$ with class excess three. The other hypotheses descend too: projective simplicity is inherited by a subfamily; affine spanning descends under the projection; coordinate-fullness descends through the free product.

name: free_product_full_dual_decomposition
statement: Let $A=\{\pm1\}\times A'$ span $\mathbb R\oplus V'$ and suppose $g(s,x)=as+g'(x)$ is sign-valued on $A$. For every $x\in A'$ both $a+g'(x)$ and $-a+g'(x)$ lie in $\{\pm1\}$; therefore either $a=0$ and $g'$ is sign-valued on $A'$, or $|a|=1$ and $g'$ vanishes on the spanning set $A'$, so $g=\pm s$. Hence the projective full dual of a free product is exactly the disjoint union of the free coordinate and the full dual of the reduced factor.
notes: Consequence: deleting or reinserting free coordinates creates NO hidden full-dual form. This is what justifies every occurrence of 'after zero Gale columns are deleted' in the finite reduction -- a hypothesis-preservation lemma, not just a counting one.

name: spanning_homogenization_lemma
statement: If $S_t$ affinely spans its expected $r$-dimensional affine solution space, then $\widehat A_t=\{(x,1):x\in S_t\}\cup\{(-x,-1):x\in S_t\}=\widehat W\cap\{\pm1\}^{m+1}$ linearly spans $\widehat W=\ker[C\mid-t]$. Proof: fix $x_0\in S_t$; the differences $x-x_0$ span $\ker C$, so the lifts span $\ker C\times\{0\}$ and $(x_0,1)$, whose sum has dimension $r+1=m-2=\dim\widehat W$.

name: intrinsic_cube_model_closure_lemma
statement: Assume affine spanning and coordinate-full homogenization; put $R=\dim\widehat W=m-2$, $M=m+1$. Then after a linear choice of intrinsic coordinates, $\widehat A_t$ becomes an antipodal spanning subset $A\subset\{\pm1\}^R$ (tag 6) which is full closed and whose projective full dual satisfies $|D(A)|=M=R+3$ (tag 7).
notes: Proof: choose $R$ independent full-dual members as a basis and let $\Phi(w)=(g_1(w),\dots,g_R(w))$ (tag 8), a linear isomorphism mapping $\widehat A_t$ into the intrinsic cube. The $M$ displayed homogenized coordinate forms are projectively distinct (if $\widehat f_i=\pm h$ on $\widehat W$, restriction to $U=\ker h=\ker C\times\{0\}$ would give $f_i=0$ on $\ker C$, contradicting old projective simplicity). Closure: if $y\in\operatorname{cl}(A)$ and $w=\Phi^{-1}(y)$, every displayed coordinate of $w$ is a sign, so $w\in\widehat W\cap\{\pm1\}^M=\widehat A_t$.

name: forced_exceptional_plane_prop_4_1
statement: Assume (1) $S_t$ affinely spans its expected affine flat; (2) the old coordinate family is projectively simple; (3) the homogenization is coordinate-full; (4) $d_{\rm geo}(F)=3$; (5) the homogeneous relation-corank-three theorem gives $d_{\rm geo}(\widehat F)\le2$ (tag 11). name: exact_full_dual_algorithm
statement: exact_full_dual(points): compute $r=\operatorname{qrank}(\text{points})$, greedily keep $r$ coordinates on which the projection still has rank $r$, take $r$ independent projected points as a basis, and for each tail in $\{\pm1\}^{r-1}$ set values $=(1,\text{tail})$, solve $Bh=\text{values}$ exactly over $\mathbb Q$, and accept the form iff $|\langle x,h\rangle|=1$ for EVERY projected point $x$. Returns the accepted value-vectors as the projective full dual in evaluation coordinates.
notes: Normalization to first evaluation $=1$ is exactly the projective quotient by $\pm1$; enumerating tails is complete because a full-dual form is determined by its values on a basis of the fibre. This makes the full dual computable exactly, which is the pivot on which the whole finite programme rests.

name: residual_certificate_search_algorithm
statement: quotient_classes(forms, residual): $i\sim j$ iff for some sign $\sigma$, $\operatorname{qrank}(\text{residual}\cup\{f_i-\sigma f_j\})=\operatorname{qrank}(\text{residual})$. residual_certificate(forms, target): if $|\text{forms}|\le r$ return the trivial certificate; otherwise enumerate all canonical signed-difference directions $f_i-\sigma f_j$ and, for $d=1,\dots,\text{target}$, test every $d$-subset of independent directions, returning the first whose quotient has at most $r=\operatorname{qrank}(\text{forms})$ classes.
notes: Exhaustive over signed-difference residuals of dimension $\le$ target, so a NEGATIVE result (None) is a proof that $d_{\rm geo}>$ target within the signed-difference class -- this is what makes the checker a certificate producer in both directions.

name: primal_forms_integer_coordinate_rows
statement: primal_forms(cols): given $m$ columns in $\mathbb Z^3$, pick three with nonzero $3\times3$ determinant as pivots; for each free index $j$, set $\text{forms}[j][z]=\det(\text{pivot matrix})$ and $\text{forms}[\text{pivot}_k][z]=\det$ of the pivot matrix with row $k$ replaced by $-\text{cols}[j]$. Returns exact INTEGER coordinate rows for the coordinate forms on $\ker C$.
notes: Cramer/adjugate construction -- the integer analogue of the $g=\operatorname{adj}(B)v/\det B$ repair S3 prescribes for the floating-point C++ routines. It is why the $m=8$ part of the checker was already safe.
